title: Git in one minute (the undo button for code)
description:
Byte finally understands why Compy commits so often. Git saves snapshots you can go back to.

#git #coding #programming #shorts
angle: Git is an undo button because every commit is a full snapshot you can return to, even after a mistake.
hook: Be honest. Have you ever named a file final_v3_REAL_final.py?

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Be honest. Have you ever named a file final_v3_REAL_final.py?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Yes, and today's episode is for you. Three things: snapshots, undoing, and the safety net.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: So git is just a folder of renamed copies. Final, final2, final_real.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Close, but git does it properly. Each commit is a snapshot of your whole project, with a message attached.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: And when I break everything at two in the morning?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: You go back to the last snapshot that worked. Nothing is lost, as long as you committed.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: What if I already committed the disaster?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Revert adds a new commit that undoes the bad one. History stays honest, and so do you.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: And if I delete a whole branch by accident?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: The reflog remembers where you were. Git keeps those entries for about ninety days by default.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: So the rule is simple: commit early, commit small.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Follow for more. Next up: hash tables, or how a dictionary finds things instantly.

props.next: Hash tables, the dictionary that never searches

claims.text: Git stores a project's history as snapshots (commits) of the full set of files
git reflog records where HEAD and branch tips have been so lost commits can be recovered; entries expire after 90 days by default
git revert records a new commit that undoes the changes of earlier commits
